title: Annual and spring flow timing trends had uncertain differences at Lena and Ob in certified 1980-2011 records
abstract: We tested whether annual flow timing misses earlier April-July flow at Lena-Kyusyur and Ob-Salekhard, with Yenisey-Igarka as a published benchmark. ArcticGRO v20261104 gave 31 common certified years from 1980 to 2011 after exclusion of incomplete 2000. Annual-minus-spring midpoint trends were +1.58 days per decade at Lena and +1.18 at Ob. Their two-test adjusted intervals were -1.09 to +4.20 and -0.92 to +3.39. Thus neither new basin gave a clear timing trend gap under the main test. The Yenisey benchmark was +1.03, with marginal 95% limits +0.28 to +1.81. No between-basin slope difference was clear. Seasonal-share and within-season-shape effects also had intervals across zero in a descriptive period-curve test. Volume weighting did not change that result. A 1990 start and an extension through provisional 2023 values gave positive Lena gap intervals, so the primary result does not establish no gap. The record is short, flow is regulated, and uncertainty omits measurement and revision errors. No physical cause or ocean response is identified. Code, a plan, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit permit reproduction from fixed external source files.

display.caption: Timing trends and seasonal accounting for 31 common certified years, 1980-2011, excluding 2000. Annual-minus-spring trend intervals include zero at Lena and Ob after two-test adjustment. The Yenisey series is a prior benchmark. Panel C gives descriptive period-curve accounting; every component interval includes zero.

citations.reason: The published Yenisey timing gap sets the question. We test new basin records in a shorter matched certified period. Yenisey is a benchmark, not a new discovery.
We apply its seasonal-share and within-season-shape accounting method with new code, other basin records and a planned volume-weighting check.
